statement: On a square grid, the point M at (5, 3) is exactly halfway between the point A at (2, 1) and another point B. Where is B?

choices.misconception: I found the move from A to M, 3 right and 2 up, and gave that move as if it were the point B.
I found the point halfway between A and M, instead of the point B that M is halfway to.
I found the right point but wrote its two numbers the wrong way round.
I added the numbers of A and M, 2 + 5 and 1 + 3, instead of repeating the move from A to M.

hints: How do you get from A to M on the grid?
Describe the move from A to M as so many right and so many up. Because M is exactly halfway, the move from M on to B is the same move again.
From (2, 1) to (5, 3) is 3 right and 2 up. Make that same move again, starting from (5, 3).

solutions.reliable: From A at (2, 1) to M at (5, 3) is 3 right and 2 up. Because M is exactly halfway between A and B, the move from M to B is the same: 3 right and 2 up from (5, 3) reaches (8, 5). Check: 5 is halfway between 2 and 8, and 3 is halfway between 1 and 5, so M really is the middle point. The transferable idea: on a grid, describe the move between two points; halfway means the same move made twice.
solutions.elegant: Each number of M is halfway between the matching numbers of A and B. The first number of B is 5 + (5 - 2) = 8 and the second is 3 + (3 - 1) = 5, so B is (8, 5).

whyOnTest: Lattice questions reward describing a move as so many right and so many up; halfway means the move from the middle to the far end copies the move from the start.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
